headline: CODELCO ADMITS 42,100 TONNES OF INFLATED COPPER OUTPUT — INTERNAL CONTROLS BREACH CLOUDS CHILE SUPPLY DATA
snippet: Chile's Codelco, the world's largest copper miner, identified 42,100 tonnes of artificially inflated production data in its reporting, exposing a significant internal controls failure at the state-owned giant. The scale of the inflation raises serious questions about the reliability of Chile's official copper output figures — a country that accounts for roughly 24% of global mined copper supply. Analysts and traders who rely on Codelco's output data to model global supply-demand balances will need to revisit historical figures, and the revelation could force a rethink of the assumed physical tightness in copper markets that has underpinned bullish price views.

headline: FREEPORT GREENLIGHTS $4.5B BAGDAD ARIZONA EXPANSION — AMERICA'S LARGEST COPPER MINER DOUBLES DOWN
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan approved a $4.5 billion expansion of its Bagdad copper mine in Arizona, designed to roughly double the asset's copper production capacity. The move is the most significant domestic copper capital commitment in years and signals Freeport's confidence that long-term demand from AI data centre power, electrification, and domestic manufacturing policy will support the project's economics despite near-term price volatility near $14,000/t. Arizona's established permitting regime and Freeport's existing operational footprint at Bagdad reduce execution risk relative to greenfield development, though the $4.5B capex will weigh on near-term free cash flow as copper prices remain unsettled.

headline: IVANHOE MINES FACES SECOND KAMOA-KAKULA PRODUCTION DOWNGRADE — DRC RAMP DELAYS HIT WORLD'S RICHEST COPPER DEPOSIT
snippet: Ivanhoe Mines is facing a second consecutive production downgrade at Kamoa-Kakula in the Democratic Republic of Congo, one of the world's highest-grade copper deposits. The delay sets back the asset's recovery timeline from earlier operational challenges and pushes out the anticipated ramp toward 500,000+ tonnes per annum capacity. Repeated guidance cuts have frustrated investors who built positions on the ramp story, and the revised schedule adds pressure on Ivanhoe shares at a time when copper prices are already under strain from AI-sector volatility and macro headwinds. DRC political and logistics risk continues to discount what is otherwise one of the world's most compelling copper development stories.

headline: RIO TINTO OPENS TWO ARGENTINA LITHIUM PROJECTS — $1.4B LITHIUM TRIANGLE BET MADE AT THE BOTTOM OF THE CYCLE
snippet: Rio Tinto formally opened two lithium projects in Argentina backed by approximately C$2 billion (~$1.4 billion USD) in combined investment, making it one of the largest new entrants to the Lithium Triangle. The timing is aggressive: Rio is committing production capital at a moment when Citi has just slashed lithium price forecasts by 40% to $12,000/t and Albemarle is warning on Q4 revenues. The company appears to be making a medium-term demand bet — EV adoption and stationary energy storage are expected to drive lithium demand regardless of near-term price weakness — while accepting that project economics will be pressured until the current oversupply cycle clears, likely 2027-2028 on most analyst timelines.

headline: ALBEMARLE WARNS Q4 LITHIUM REVENUE TO FALL — CEO FLAGS 48% DEMAND SURGE BUT PRICES WON'T FOLLOW
snippet: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB), the world's largest lithium producer, warned that Q4 2026 revenues will decline from Q3 as lithium prices remain depressed — reinforcing the structural price pressure behind Citi's recent 40% forecast cut. In a striking contrast, Albemarle's CEO disclosed that global lithium demand rose 48% in the year to August 2026, driven by EVs and stationary energy storage. The demand-price paradox — rocketing volumes, collapsing prices — reflects a market where new capacity additions from Australia, Chile and Argentina are running faster than demand growth. For TSX-V lithium juniors, the signal is blunt: strong demand numbers will not revive underwater development projects while spot prices hover near $12,000/t.

headline: CRITICAL METALS CORP HITS NASDAQ AFTER EUROPEAN LITHIUM MERGER — GREENLAND REE DEPOSIT NOW U.S.-LISTED
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRTM) began trading on the Nasdaq on November 6 following completion of its court-approved merger with European Lithium, effective November 5. The combined entity brings together rare earth assets at the Tanbreez deposit in Greenland — one of the largest undeveloped rare earth deposits outside China — with European lithium exposure. The Nasdaq listing gives the company access to U.S. institutional capital at a moment when Washington is actively incentivising domestic rare earth supply chains and the approaching expiry of China's export control pause (November 10) is focusing investor attention on alternative Western supply. CRTM is now one of a handful of pure-play critical minerals juniors listed on a major U.S. exchange.

headline: TRUMP CRITICAL MINERALS DEALS ROCKED BY MIDTERM BLUE WAVE — EVEN GOP BREAKS ON CHINA CONCESSIONS
snippet: Critical minerals agreements struck under the Trump administration are facing mounting political pressure in the wake of the November midterm elections, with opposition now coming from within the Republican Party as well as Democrats. The deals, which involved trade concessions with China over rare earth and critical mineral export controls, are under scrutiny from Congressional members on both sides, raising uncertainty over whether agreements underpinning market stability for materials including rare earths, cobalt, and lithium will hold into 2027. For junior mining investors, the political risk is now additive to the existing price and demand uncertainty in the sector — particularly for projects seeking government financing or offtake support.

headline: FORTUNA MINING CONFIRMS 64M AT 1.9 G/T GOLD IN SENEGAL — KABEWEST ZONE GROWS AT BAMBADJI
snippet: Fortuna Mining (NYSE: FSM) reported an intersection of 64 metres grading 1.9 g/t gold at the Kabewest zone of its Bambadji Project in Senegal in a November 2 release, confirming broad, continuous gold mineralization within the project's exploration licence. While 1.9 g/t over 64m is not headline-grade, the width and consistency suggest a potential bulk-tonnage open-pit target that could complement Fortuna's existing producing assets. Fortuna is a mid-tier gold and silver producer with operations in Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Peru and Argentina, and is adding West Africa exploration exposure at a time when the region is attracting increased major miner interest.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS TANKS 12% TO $7.25 — SECTOR ROUT DEEPENS AS CHINA EXPIRY LOOMS AND PRICES SLIDE
snippet: Rare Earths Americas shares fell 12% to $7.25 at Thursday's close in New York, valuing the company at approximately $149 million, as a broad sector selloff extended into the week. The decline is part of a wider rare earth equities rout: MP Materials has shed 53% from its 52-week high and fell 11.9% in October alone amid concerns that China's expanded export controls — whose pause expires November 10 — will resume and disrupt U.S. magnet supply chains that have not yet been fully diversified. Junior rare earth developers on the TSX-V and ASX are caught between China-driven supply risk (which should theoretically boost their value) and a market that is punishing any mining equity not generating near-term cash flow.

headline: MOSAIC MINERALS DRILLS INTO GOLDEN ISLAND — 72.8 G/T GOLD AT SURFACE TRIGGERS 2,000-METRE MAIDEN DRILL IN QUÉBEC
snippet: Mosaic Minerals (TSX-V) reported surface samples grading up to 72.8 g/t gold, 42.5 g/t silver, and 0.42% copper from its Golden Island project in Quebec, and has launched a maiden drilling campaign of at least 2,000 metres. High-grade gold at surface is a classic junior exploration trigger — it validates system existence and has historically attracted retail and institutional attention to Quebec-based gold juniors in the James Bay and Abitibi corridors. The addition of silver and copper in the sample suite suggests potential polymetallic mineralization. With the Quebec government actively supporting exploration through CONSOREM and SIDEX, Golden Island adds to a busy exploration season in one of the world's premier mining jurisdictions.
